quarterly_data.quarter: Toray results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY ending March 2027 conference call Q&A summary (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A, director Yuichiro Kato, Q1 of the fiscal year ending March 2027) on Performance Chemicals: Q1 benefited from expanded engineering-plastics sales, demand brought forward on Middle East concerns and an inventory valuation effect (not quantifiable by sub-segment), which helped resins & chemicals. From Q2 the inventory effect falls away and the pull-forward demand normalizes - the first-half outlook already assumes this; resin market prices for some products are expected to fall, the lactam market to deteriorate, and Soda Aromatic's profit contribution ends from Q2 after the share sale. These factors are not large in films and electronic & information materials: in films, MLCC release-film demand is expected to stay firm, and in electronic & information materials the company expects sales of materials for power inductor coils, launched in South Korea, to expand.

quarterly_data.quarter: Toray results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY ending March 2027 conference call Q&A summary (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on raw-material and fuel cost pass-through: since April the company has applied a surcharge-like mechanism to pass on cost increases as quickly as possible. Resins & chemicals passed costs on with customers' understanding and broadly kept their spread; films lag slightly behind resins and chemicals but pass-through is progressing firmly and should catch up; in Carbon Fiber Composite Materials, long-term and formula contracts mean pass-through takes some time and is expected to progress going forward.

quarterly_data.quarter: Toray results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY ending March 2027 conference call Q&A summary (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on Carbon Fiber Composite Materials: the company's material shipments for the 787 ran at a rate equivalent to 9 aircraft per month in Q1, roughly in line with its initial outlook. A major customer has explained that 787 production stabilized at about 8 per month, with some line adjustments due to engine supply delays, and that it keeps its policy of moving to 10 per month, timing depending on engine supply; Toray's own outlook is unchanged from the start of the year. Regular-tow pressure-vessel demand is bottoming as supply-chain inventory adjustment progresses, with recovery expected from Q2; large-tow wind-blade shipments have been recovering since Q1; aerospace sales keep rising, though a temporary profit boost in Q4 of the company's fiscal year 25 makes Q1 profit growth look relatively small.
quarterly_data.figure: 787 material shipments equivalent to 9 aircraft per month in Q1; customer's 787 production about 8 per month, plan to move to 10 per month

quarterly_data.quarter: Toray results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY ending March 2027 conference call Q&A summary (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on Fibers & Textiles: holding Q1 apparel profit flat year on year despite rising raw-material and fuel costs is seen as an achievement (apparel prices are often set by season). Industrial-use gains came from product mix, an improvement in airbag applications, the ramp-up of Ultrasuede artificial leather for a new program, airbag sales expansion, improvements in aramid fiber and PP spunbond in South Korea, and domestic industrial materials (partly demand brought forward). Q2 sales and profit are expected to rise from Q1 as autumn/winter apparel demand picks up; Ultrasuede should stay firm, subsidiary Alcantara expects higher sales for large programs, PP spunbond is improving through restructuring and airbag applications keep expanding.

quarterly_data.quarter: Toray results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY ending March 2027 conference call Q&A summary (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on water treatment: Q1 logistics were affected - raw-material procurement took longer and logistics around the Strait of Hormuz were disrupted, and congestion on alternative routes may still slightly affect deliveries. The company changed production sites by destination to keep supplying customers, for example shipping from Japan products originally planned to be supplied from its Saudi Arabia site, and believes it secured sales; logistics uncertainty remains.
